comparison: Strong agreement on claims C30-C34 regarding PE purity remaining largely unchanged despite increased pure PE frequencies. Both evaluations mark these claims as SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers explicitly noting 'Overall mutagenesis frequency, as measured by indel formation, increased along with increased precise PE.'

Complete agreement on background/definitional claims C1, C2, C7-C13 about PE technology and its limitations. Both evaluations mark these as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers confirm the established context without questioning these foundational claims.

Strong agreement on claims C6, C35-C40 regarding RTT +2 mutation strategy. Both evaluations mark these as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers describe these methods as 'remarkably straightforward and proved beneficial for most of the pegRNAs tested.'

Agreement on claims C14-C19 regarding pegRNA misfolding hypothesis and PBS mutations. Both evaluations mark these as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers describe the data as 'solid and convincing' and acknowledge the autoinhibitory activity findings.

Significant disagreement on claims C5, C24-C28 regarding pure PE frequency improvements. OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED, but peer reviewers mark as UNCERTAIN, noting 'The observed increases in the frequency of precise PE were relatively minor and inconsistent' and that 'prime editing activity remained relatively low for a significant proportion of pegRNAs tested.'

Agreement on claim C44 regarding combined effect of both strategies. Both evaluations mark as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers describe the methods as 'important advances' and note they 'may lead to significant improvements in editing efficiencies.'
Agreement on claims C12-C13 regarding motivation for improving PE efficiency. Both evaluations mark as SUPPORTED as part of the established background context.
Agreement on claims C41-C42 regarding refolded pegRNAs with RTT +2 mutations inducing higher indel frequencies. Both evaluations mark as SUPPORTED as part of the overall methodological advance.

Agreement on claims C3-C4, C20-C23 regarding refolding strategy and in vitro competition assay data. OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers acknowledge these findings as part of the solid data on autoinhibitory activity.

Partial overlap on claims C20-C23. OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED based on consistent improvements across target sites. Peer reviewers acknowledge the data but express concerns about overall low editing efficiency in their evaluation of related claims.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding claims C46-C47 about broader applicability. OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN noting 'speculative inferences about applicability to other systems.' Peer reviewers also mark as UNCERTAIN, noting concerns about practical utility and lack of germline transmission data.

Disagreement on claims C54-C57 regarding implications for pegRNA design. OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED, describing them as 'logical inferences appropriately framed as possibilities.' Peer reviewers mark as UNCERTAIN, questioning practical utility and broader applications.
OpenEval evaluated claims C48-C50 regarding citations to prior work as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific citation accuracy claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C58-C61 regarding methodological descriptions and ethical approval as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological detail claims.
